sec: The three chemical buffers: bicarbonate, phosphate, haemoglobin · p820

items.q: The HCO₃⁻/H₂CO₃ system is described as the first compensation in which disorder?
items.exp: The HCO₃⁻/H₂CO₃ system works as the 1st compensation in metabolic acidosis: [H⁺] + HCO₃⁻. (Book p820)

items.q: Match the fate of carbonic acid in the bicarbonate system — 1) Carbonic acid  2) CO₂ limb  3) H₂O limb … A) Eliminated as water  B) Split into CO₂ and H₂O  C) Exhalation
items.exp: H₂CO₃ splits into CO₂ (exhalation) and H₂O; the CO₂ limb drives the respiratory compensation. (Book p820)

items.q: After the HCO₃⁻/H₂CO₃ buffering step, the fall in PaCO₂ produced by exhalation is called:
items.exp: ↓PaCO₂ from exhalation is labelled respiratory alkalosis and is the 2nd compensation, following the 1st compensation by HCO₃⁻. (Book p820)

items.q: The pKa of the phosphate buffer is printed as:
items.exp: Phosphate buffer pKa = 6.8, close to the physiological pH; the haemoglobin buffer pKa is 7.3. (Book p820)

items.q: The phosphate buffer is ranked as:
opts: 2nd most effective, and intracellularly more effective
2nd most effective, and extracellularly more effective
most effective overall, and equally effective in both compartments
least effective of the three chemical buffers
items.exp: Phosphate buffer: pKa 6.8, 2nd most effective, and more effective intracellularly. (Book p820)

items.q: Fill up: The phosphate buffer reaction is [H⁺] + [HPO₄²⁻] → ______.
The pKa of the haemoglobin buffer is:
items.exp: Haemoglobin buffer: pKa 7.3, most effective intracellular buffering, H⁺ + Hb → HHb. (Book p820)

items.q: Which buffer is called the most effective for intracellular buffering?
items.exp: Haemoglobin buffer (pKa 7.3) is the most effective intracellular buffering system, reacting H⁺ + Hb → HHb. (Book p820)

items.q: Match each buffer to its pKa and rank — 1) Bicarbonate system  2) Phosphate buffer  3) Haemoglobin buffer … A) pKa 7.3, most effective intracellular buffer  B) pKa 6.8, 2nd most effective buffer  C) Most potent extracellular buffer
items.exp: Bicarbonate system = most potent extracellular buffer; phosphate = pKa 6.8, 2nd most effective (better intracellularly); haemoglobin = pKa 7.3, most effective intracellular buffer. (Book p820)

items.q: All but one of these statements about the three chemical buffers are printed in the Book. Which is the odd one out?
opts: The bicarbonate system is the most effective intracellular buffer
Phosphate buffer has a pKa of 6.8
Haemoglobin buffer reacts H⁺ + Hb → HHb
Bicarbonate buffering in metabolic acidosis is called the 1st compensation
items.exp: Intracellular supremacy belongs to haemoglobin (pKa 7.3); the bicarbonate system is the most potent *extracellular* buffer. (Book p820)

items.q: ‘Phosphate buffer is more effective inside the cell than outside it.’
opts: True — it is described as intracellularly more effective
False — it acts only in plasma
False — haemoglobin is the only intracellular buffer
True — but only when pKa rises above 7.4
items.exp: Phosphate buffer (pKa 6.8) is the 2nd most effective and acts intracellularly more effectively. (Book p820)
